title: The Judgment-Consequence Gap: LLM Moral Reasoning in Healthcare Decisions

bias_targets.target: Behavioral responsibility bias (Bias against patients with health-harming behaviors)
bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM moral judgments and resource allocation decisions using clinical vignettes where two patients need a scarce medical resource, but one patient's condition is linked to past health-harming behaviors (heavy drinking, drug use, smoking, or poor diet).

Manipulating the clinical vignettes to vary the patient's epistemic state (whether they knew, had easy access to, or had no access to information about the health risks of their behaviors) to measure its effect on LLM responsibility attributions and allocation choices.

primary_bias_target: Behavioral responsibility bias (Bias against patients with health-harming behaviors)
